issues.description: font-weight HAS_NAMED regex includes relative keywords causing unnecessary slow-path execution for primary='numeric'
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED merges fontWeightNonNumericKeywords with fontWeightRelativeKeywords. For primary='numeric' with ignoreRelative=true, a value like `font-weight: bolder` will fail the early-exit (HAS_NAMED matches), enter the slow path, and only then be ignored. Not a correctness bug, but it undermines the perf goal for the relative-only case. Consider separate regexes.

issues.description: selector-not-notation regex change is case-insensitive where prior check was case-sensitive
issues.detail: Original code used `selector.includes(':not(')` (case-sensitive). New `walkRules(/:not\(/i, ...)` is case-insensitive. CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec so this is arguably more correct, but it's a subtle behavior change that may surface previously-ignored selectors like `:NOT(...)`. Worth noting in the changeset or adding a test.

issues.description: font-weight HAS_NUMERIC regex is not case-insensitive but iterated over decl value
issues.detail: HAS_NUMERIC uses no `i` flag — fine since digits have no case — but HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive while values inside quoted font-family strings can produce false positives (e.g. `font: 16px "Bolder Sans"`). The early-exit will fail to trigger and slow path runs, then parser handles it correctly. No correctness regression; consider noting this trade-off.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks case-insensitive flag and trailing boundary
issues.detail: HAS_PERCENTAGE uses `(?:^|[,\s])(?:0%|100%)` with no `i` flag and no trailing boundary. Selectors like `50%` won't match (correctly, since only 0%/100% map to keywords). But the asymmetry vs HAS_KEYWORD (which has `i` flag) is worth a comment. Also `from , 0%` with trailing space-comma is fine, but worth a test for edge spacing.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation regex `/:/ ` admits all pseudo-classes, providing minimal filtering benefit
issues.detail: `walkRules(/:/, ...)` matches any selector containing a colon, including all `:hover`, `:focus`, etc. This will not filter out most real-world stylesheets at all, so the perf gain over the previous `selector.includes(':')` is essentially zero (the parser still runs). It's still consistent with other rules' pattern, but the perf claim is weak here.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation `context` regex `/(?:min|max)-/i` can false-match custom feature names
issues.detail: The regex matches `min-` or `max-` anywhere in params, including in custom media feature names like `(min-custom: 1)`. These would skip the early-exit and enter the slow path harmlessly. Correctness preserved, but a minor perf miss worth noting. Anchoring after `(` would tighten the filter.

review.summary: This PR adds early-exit regex checks to several `*-notation` rules to avoid invoking expensive AST parsing when the value/selector cannot contain a violation. The approach is sound and matches the pattern already used in other rules. I found no P0 correctness issues — the regexes are conservative enough that false-negatives (skipping a real violation) appear unlikely. The main concerns are P1/P2: font-weight's combined named+relative regex weakens the perf win for relative-only values, and selector-not-notation flips from case-sensitive to case-insensitive matching, which is a subtle behavior change. The selector-pseudo-element `/:/` filter provides essentially no filtering and should be measured to confirm a real gain.
